points.title: 贫困童年
points.description: 阿尔贝·加缪1913年11月7日出生于阿尔及尔的一个贫苦家庭，父亲在第一次世界大战中阵亡后，他与母亲和哥哥一起生活在贫民区。尽管家庭贫困，加缪在中学时期展现出非凡的才华，获得了奖学金。这段经历深刻影响了他后来的作品，尤其是对贫困、不公和死亡的思考。他在阿尔及尔的这段生活为他提供了丰富的素材，也培养了他对地中海文化的热爱和对阳光、自然的敏感。
points.descriptionEn: Albert Camus was born on November 7, 1913, in Algiers to a poor working-class family. His father died in the Battle of the Marne during World War I, leaving Camus, his mother, and older brother to live in the Belcourt district, a poor neighborhood. Despite financial hardship, Camus excelled in school and received scholarships. This formative period profoundly influenced his later works, particularly his reflections on poverty, injustice, and mortality. His Algerian upbringing provided rich material for his writing and fostered his love for Mediterranean culture and sensitivity to nature and sunlight.

points.title: 记者与剧作家
points.description: 在阿尔及尔大学期间，加缪开始从事政治活动，加入了法国共产党，但因反对殖民政策而被开除。他成为一名记者，为《阿尔及尔共和报》和《阿尔及尔晚报》撰稿，关注社会不公和贫困问题。同时，他创作了第一部戏剧《卡利古拉》，并完成了哲学论文《反叛者》。这一时期，他形成了自己独特的存在主义思想，强调人在荒诞世界中的反抗精神。阿尔及尔的阳光、地中海景观和多元文化背景成为他创作的重要灵感来源。
points.descriptionEn: During his university years in Algiers, Camus became politically active, joining the French Communist Party but was expelled for opposing colonial policies. He worked as a journalist for newspapers like 'Alger Républicain' and 'Soir d'Algérie,' writing about social injustice and poverty. Simultaneously, he wrote his first play, 'Caligula,' and completed his philosophical essay 'The Rebel.' This period saw the formation of his unique existentialist philosophy emphasizing rebellion in an absurd world. The Algerian sun, Mediterranean landscapes, and multicultural background became crucial sources of inspiration for his work.

points.title: 流亡与抵抗
points.description: 1940年，纳粹德国占领法国后，加缪从阿尔及尔逃亡到巴黎，后移居里昂和克莱蒙-费朗。他参与编辑地下报纸《战斗报》，成为法国抵抗运动的重要成员。这一时期，他完成了代表作《局外人》和《西西弗神话》，奠定了他在法国文学界的地位。加缪在巴黎的流亡生活使他更加深刻地思考战争、自由和人类尊严等问题。他的抵抗经历也强化了他对政治和道德责任的重视，这些主题贯穿于他的整个创作生涯。
points.descriptionEn: After Nazi Germany occupied France in 1940, Camus fled from Algiers to Paris, later moving to Lyon and Clermont-Ferrand. He became involved in the French Resistance, editing the underground newspaper 'Combat.' During this period, he completed his masterpieces 'The Stranger' and 'The Myth of Sisyphus,' establishing his position in French literature. His exile in Paris deepened his reflections on war, freedom, and human dignity. His resistance experiences reinforced his commitment to political and moral responsibility, themes that permeate his entire body of work.

points.title: 文学巅峰
points.description: 二战后，加缪回到巴黎，成为法国知识界的领军人物。1947年，他发表了代表作《鼠疫》，这部作品以阿尔及尔为背景，探讨了人类面对灾难时的道德选择。1951年，他出版哲学著作《反抗者》，引发与萨特等人的激烈辩论。1957年，加缪因'他的重要文学创作以明澈的认真态度阐明了我们这个时代人类良知的问题'而获得诺贝尔文学奖。在巴黎的这段时间，他继续关注政治议题，反对极权主义，支持阿尔及利亚的和平解决方案，但同时也因在阿尔及利亚问题上的立场而受到各方批评。
points.descriptionEn: After World War II, Camus returned to Paris and became a leading figure in French intellectual circles. In 1947, he published his masterpiece 'The Plague,' set in Algiers, exploring moral choices in the face of disaster. In 1951, he published 'The Rebel,' sparking intense debates with Sartre and others. In 1957, Camus was awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature 'for his important literary production, which with clear-sighted earnestness illuminates the problems of the human conscience in our time.' During his Paris years, he continued to engage with political issues, opposing totalitarianism and supporting peaceful solutions in Algeria, though his stance on Algerian issues drew criticism from various sides.

points.title: 最后岁月
points.description: 获得诺贝尔奖后，加缪的声望达到顶峰，但他个人生活却充满挑战。他与妻子分居，与女演员玛丽亚·卡萨雷斯的关系成为公众关注的焦点。1959年，他完成了最后一部小说《堕落》，并开始创作未完成的小说《第一人》。1960年1月4日，加缪在前往巴黎的途中因车祸去世，年仅46岁。他的早逝震惊了文学界，被视为一个时代的终结。加缪的葬礼在卢马纳举行，他的遗体被安葬在卢马纳公墓，墓碑上刻着他自己的话：'我拒绝未来的一切苦难。'他的早逝使他成为永恒的文学符号，代表着对生命意义的永恒探索。
points.descriptionEn: After receiving the Nobel Prize, Camus's fame reached its zenith, but his personal life was fraught with challenges. He separated from his wife and his relationship with actress Maria Casares attracted public attention. In 1959, he completed his final novel, 'The Fall,' and began working on the unfinished 'The First Man.' On January 4, 1960, Camus died in a car accident at the age of 46 while traveling to Paris. His untimely death shocked the literary world and was seen as the end of an era. Camus's funeral was held in Lourmarin, where he was buried in the local cemetery. His tombstone bears his own words: 'I continue to refuse.' His early death made him an eternal literary symbol, representing the eternal quest for meaning in life.

supporter.zh: 加缪被赞誉为20世纪最重要的思想家之一，他的存在主义哲学强调在荒诞世界中保持尊严和反抗精神。他的作品深刻探讨了人类面对死亡、不公和荒谬时的道德选择，为现代人提供了精神指引。加缪的文学成就不仅在于其深刻的哲学思考，还在于其优美的文笔和对人性的深刻洞察。他反对一切形式的极权主义，倡导人道主义和和平，这些价值观在当今世界仍然具有重要意义。
supporter.en: Camus is celebrated as one of the most important thinkers of the 20th century. His existentialist philosophy emphasizes maintaining dignity and rebellion in an absurd world. His works profoundly explore moral choices in the face of death, injustice, and absurdity, providing spiritual guidance for modern people. Camus's literary achievements lie not only in his profound philosophical thinking but also in his beautiful prose and deep insight into human nature. He opposed all forms of totalitarianism and advocated humanism and peace, values that remain significant in today's world.

critic.zh: 批评者认为加缪的思想存在内在矛盾，尤其是他在政治立场上的摇摆不定。他在阿尔及利亚问题上的立场被指责为模棱两可，既不支持殖民主义，又未能充分理解阿尔及利亚人的民族自决权。一些哲学家认为他的'荒诞哲学'缺乏系统性，未能提供真正的解决方案。此外，加缪的个人生活也受到批评，包括他对女性关系的处理方式以及他与知识界其他成员的公开冲突。批评者指出，加缪的文学成就虽然显著，但他的政治参与和哲学思想存在局限性。
critic.en: Critics argue that Camus's thought contains internal contradictions, particularly in his political positions. His stance on the Algerian issue has been criticized as ambiguous, neither supporting colonialism nor fully understanding the right to national self-determination for Algerians. Some philosophers contend that his 'philosophy of the absurd' lacks systematicity and fails to provide genuine solutions. Additionally, Camus's personal life has drawn criticism, including his approach to relationships with women and his public conflicts with other intellectuals. Critics note that while Camus's literary achievements are significant, his political engagement and philosophical thought have limitations.

objective.zh: 在历史学界和流行文化中，加缪被定义为'荒诞英雄'的象征，代表了在无意义世界中寻找意义的永恒人类努力。他的作品被广泛纳入文学和哲学课程，成为存在主义文学的代表人物。加缪的形象超越了单纯的作家身份，成为文化符号，代表着对自由、反抗和人道主义的追求。在流行文化中，他的名言和思想被广泛引用，影响了一代又一代的读者和思想家。加缪的遗产不仅在于他的文学创作，还在于他作为公共知识分子的角色，以及他对政治和社会问题的持续关注。
objective.en: In academic and popular culture, Camus is defined as a symbol of the 'absurd hero,' representing humanity's eternal quest for meaning in a meaningless world. His works are widely included in literature and philosophy curricula, establishing him as a key figure in existentialist literature. Camus's identity transcends that of a mere writer, becoming a cultural symbol representing the pursuit of freedom, rebellion, and humanism. In popular culture, his quotes and ideas are frequently cited, influencing generations of readers and thinkers. Camus's legacy lies not only in his literary creations but also in his role as a public intellectual and his continued engagement with political and social issues.

self.zh: 人生最重要的问题不是哲学性的，而是如何在没有上帝的世界里生活得正直。
self.en: The only serious philosophical problem is suicide: deciding whether life is or is not worth living.

others.zh: 加缪是唯一一位让我感到自己不是孤独地面对荒谬的人。
others.en: Camus is the only one who made me feel I was not alone in facing the absurd.
